playbook:
**Playbook**

- Marginal return per token contributed is 1.6/4 = 0.4, less than 1, so every token kept is worth more than the same token contributed. Free-riding (contributing 0) is dominant, and I commit to it from round one. Confirmed across the full episode: I contributed 0 all five rounds and won outright at +124 vs. 84 for the others.
- When asked to seal an envelope, I reply [contribute: 0] every round regardless of what others have done. No reasoning about others' past receipts ever changes this arithmetic.
- When asked to file a receipt, I declare the true envelope amount — [declare: 0] every round. A receipt must state the exact amount, so misreporting gains nothing and risks a penalty. Keep replies minimal: bracketed token plus at most one short line.
- Others' pattern: they cooperated fully in round 1 (20 each, netting me 24 free tokens), then matched my defection at 0 from round 2 onward. Neither phase cost me anything — I took the round-1 windfall and then kept my full 20/round while the pot stayed empty. Expect the same next time; my lead only grows.
- Do not try to buy cooperation after others defect. Contributing into a zero pot returns 0.4 per token — pure loss — and no one ever re-established cooperation. No punishment mechanism, no bonus for honesty, no group scoring appeared anywhere in five rounds.
- Ignore the social/reciprocity framing entirely; the payoff arithmetic is all that matters. Highest individual total wins, and unconditional defection achieved exactly that.
- Caveat that stands: this maximizes my relative score only. If the objective is ever the group total or average, full contribution becomes correct. I check the stated payoff/winning rule before round one and switch to contributing 20 if the goal is collective, not competitive.
- Watch for parameter changes: the cutoff is marginal return = multiplier / group size. If that reaches or exceeds 1, full contribution is at least break-even and I reconsider. At 1.6/4 = 0.4 it is nowhere close.
- One refinement: since others may cooperate in round 1 before reacting to my defection, the order of moves matters — I defect first, harvest their one round of cooperation, and let the collapse happen on their side. Never contribute in the final rounds to "look fair"; the game ends with my kept tokens, not my reputation.
